question: What was the primary focus of Florence Nightingale's data collection during the Crimean War?

options.A: Preventable infectious diseases and environmental sanitation
options.B: Surgical complication rates among frontline officers
options.D: Pharmacological efficacy of newly synthesized anesthetics

explanation: Nightingale used statistical data to prove that poor sanitary conditions and infectious diseases accounted for the vast majority of military casualties, driving early hospital reform. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h1)

question: How did Florence Nightingale's work in the Crimea fundamentally shape modern nursing?

options.A: It proved that pharmacological interventions are superior to environmental controls
options.B: It established empirical observation and data analysis as tools for clinical reform
options.C: It created the first legal framework for hospital licensure
options.D: It separated nursing administration entirely from medical oversight

explanation: By systematically tracking mortality data to advocate for environmental changes, Nightingale laid the groundwork for evidence-based nursing practice. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h1)

question: What type of publications dominated nursing literature during the early twentieth century?

options.B: Advanced epidemiological surveys on chronic illness
options.C: Descriptive case studies and procedural manuals
options.D: Randomized controlled trials on medication dosages

explanation: Early 20th-century nursing literature focused heavily on standardizing basic hospital procedures and sharing anecdotal case reports rather than formal scientific experimentation. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why was formal nursing research slow to develop during the early 1900s?

options.A: There were no patients suffering from chronic illnesses at that time
options.B: Nursing education relied heavily on hospital-based apprenticeships focused on task execution
options.C: All medical research was strictly reserved for licensed physicians
options.D: Governments legally banned nurses from conducting clinical observations

explanation: The dominant hospital-training school model trained nurses to perform duties efficiently under physician direction rather than to question, design, or execute scientific studies. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h2)

question: What milestone journal was launched in the 1950s to disseminate empirical nursing studies?
explanation: The journal Nursing Research was established in the 1950s to provide a dedicated peer-reviewed venue for publishing scientific studies conducted by nurses. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h3)

question: What was a primary catalyst for the growth of nursing research immediately following World War II?

options.A: The expansion of graduate education and doctoral training for nurses
options.B: The discovery of penicillin and universal health insurance
options.C: The immediate elimination of all physician-led hospital committees
options.D: The complete replacement of hospital diplomas with university degrees

explanation: As nurses pursued master's and doctoral degrees, they gained the formal research training necessary to design, fund, and execute scientific studies independently. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h3)

question: What was the main emphasis of nursing scholarship during the 1970s and 1980s?

options.B: Developing conceptual models and nursing theories

explanation: The 1970s and 1980s were marked by intense scholarly activity aimed at creating formal nursing theories to define the unique scope and focus of the profession. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why did nurse leaders emphasize theory development during this period?

options.A: To prove that nurses could perform complex surgical procedures
options.B: To satisfy strict international legal mandates imposed on hospitals
options.C: To establish a distinct scientific framework that separates nursing practice from general medicine
options.D: To eliminate the need for bedside clinical observations

explanation: Nursing theories provided a structured way to view patient care through a uniquely nursing lens, anchoring the profession in its own scientific body of knowledge. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following components is NOT typically included in the classical definition of evidence-based practice?

options.A: Strict adherence to traditional hospital routines

explanation: Evidence-based practice explicitly moves away from blind adherence to tradition, replacing it with research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient values. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h5)

question: How did the rise of evidence-based practice change the daily expectations placed on practicing nurses?

options.A: Nurses were expected to critically appraise research and apply findings to patient care
options.B: Nurses assumed full legal responsibility for hospital facility budgets
options.C: Nurses stopped using patient care plans entirely in favor of computer algorithms
options.D: Nurses were required to independently write and publish peer-reviewed clinical textbooks

explanation: The EBP movement shifted the nursing role from passive consumers of hospital routines to active evaluators and implementers of validated scientific research. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is a major focus area for contemporary nursing research within Nigeria?

options.A: Developing deep-sea hyperbaric diving decompression tables
options.B: Managing geriatric care facilities in sub-zero climates
options.C: Designing experimental commercial aircraft cabin interiors
options.D: Maternal and child health outcomes and resource-limited primary care

explanation: Nigerian nursing research heavily addresses pressing local health priorities, including reducing maternal mortality and optimizing primary healthcare delivery with limited resources. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is a common systemic challenge faced by nurse researchers working in many Nigerian clinical and academic settings?

options.A: Legal prohibitions against nurses reading international scientific journals
options.B: A complete absence of patients suffering from acute or chronic medical conditions
options.C: Mandatory government bans on collecting qualitative or quantitative health data
options.D: Limited funding and heavy clinical workloads that restrict time for investigation

explanation: High patient-to-nurse ratios, heavy clinical demands, and scarce grant funding frequently challenge nurses attempting to conduct research in resource-constrained environments. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h6)
